answers.question: Is it crazy to do one more 16-miler on Wednesday so I feel ready?
answers.answer: Not crazy, but no. Another 16-miler five days out would leave you running the marathon on tired legs and change nothing about your fitness. The work that gets you under 3:45 is already banked. The job this week is to arrive fresh. If you need to feel the distance, a short run with 3 or 4 miles at marathon pace on Tuesday will tell your legs the pace without costing anything.

new.analysis:
## How last week went
You followed the taper plan cleanly: five runs, 34 mi, the 8-with-4-at-marathon-pace on Wednesday, and a controlled 12 mi Sunday. Marathon-pace splits sat at 8:32 – 8:40/mi with heart rate at 147, right where sub-3:45 lives. That is the shape of a ready runner, not a fading one.

## Why the legs feel flat
Heavy and dead is what a taper feels like when it is working. Blood volume shifts, glycogen refills, little aches surface, and easy pace can feel sluggish for a few days. Your easy pace and easy heart rate have not moved for three weeks, which tells me nothing is actually lost.

## How to run the race
Start honest, not brave: the first 2 miles should feel almost too easy at 8:40 – 8:45/mi, then settle into 8:30 – 8:35/mi through 20. The race begins at mile 20, and the only way to run it is to still have legs. Take fuel every 30 to 35 minutes from the start, drink to thirst, and do not chase anyone through the first 10K.

## This week's shape
Short, easy running with a few strides and a couple of marathon-pace pickups keeps the system primed without draining it. Friday is a full rest day, Saturday is a tiny shakeout, Sunday you race. Sleep is more valuable than any run this week.
